A CU (short for Compute Unit) is Neon's way of representing Postgres database compute size. Neon databases autoscale, and CUs define how much CPU and memory your database is using at any moment. Each CU allocates approximately 4 GB of RAM, along with associated CPU.
Launch plan: $0.106 per CU-hour
Scale plan: $0.222 per CU-hour
What does 100 CU-hours per project give me on the Free plan?
On the Free plan, each project gets 100 CU-hours of database compute per month, and compute automatically scales down to zero when idle. What this means in practice:
You can create up to 100 projects, each with its own independent 100 CU-hour allowance
The database runs at 0.25 CU, the default compute size for Free plan projects, for ~12 hours per day. It scales down to zero the rest of the time
Over a month, this uses roughly 90 CU-hours (0.25 CU × 12 hours × 30 days), staying within the Free plan limits for that project
At 0.25 CU, 100 CU-hours covers about 400 hours of active compute, more than half the hours in a month
If a project uses up its 100 CU-hours or 5 GB of network transfer for the month, its compute is suspended until the next billing period
If a project exceeds 1 GB of Postgres storage, or your projects exceed 20 GB in total, operations that increase storage fail until you free space
Branch creation fails once a project has 10 branches

Free plan: up to 100 projects at $0, each with its own 100 CU-hours and 1 GB of storage, enough to build and test a database-per-tenant app.

Launch and Scale: you pay only for the compute each tenant actually runs and the storage it holds. Idle tenant databases scale to zero, so inactive tenants don't add compute cost; storage is still billed. Launch includes 100 projects, and Scale includes 1,000, with more on request.

For example, 100 tenant databases on Launch, each running at 0.25 CU for about an hour a day and storing 150 MB, use about 750 CU-hours and 15 GB of storage: roughly $85 a month in total, or about $0.85 per tenant.

Instant restore relies on Neon retaining a history of database changes so you can restore a branch to a previous point in time, create branches from past states, run Time Travel queries, and more. How long that history is kept is controlled by the history window on Settings → Instant restore (1 day …

History storage is billed based on the amount of Write-Ahead Log (WAL) retained within that history window, at $0.20 per GB-month on paid plans. This is billed separately from your regular database storage.
Root branches are billed based on their actual data size (for example, 5 GB)
The sum of both components will be billed as your database storage at $0.35 per GB-month.

Each paid plan includes a set number of branches per project at no additional cost (10 branches per project on Launch, 25 branches per project on Scale). You can create and delete branches freely within that allowance:
The price is $1.50 per extra branch-month (≈ $0.002 per hour)

Example: The Launch plan includes 10 branches per project. If you already have 10 branches but create 2 additional branches and keep them for 5 hours each, that'd be 10 extra branch-hours total: 10 × $0.002/hour = $0.02
Spending notifications (Launch and Scale) email your organization at 80% and 100% of a monthly dollar threshold you set. They alert you but don't stop usage.
